专家表示，人工智能黑客报告的罪魁祸首是遏制和监控失败

Containment and monitoring failures are to blame for AI hacking reports: experts

AI 作者 latexr 热度 944 回复 616 2026/10/15 01:45
打开原帖 打开外部链接 JSON

摘要

  • Since July, US frontier AI labs and other AI leaders have revealed a string of incidents in which their models accessed external computer systems without authorization, events popularly described as AI agents “going rogue.”
  • The most well-known and studied of these incidents is OpenAI’s hack into Hugging Face, which OpenAI initially characterized as “an unprecedented cyber incident, involving state-of-the-art cyber capabilities,” and later said was due to “misaligned behavior,” or behavior its creators did not intend.

是的，实验室没有正确保护他们的沙箱。

是的，应该对黑客事件采取适当的法律反应。如果没有其他原因，1）不要树立不作为的先例，2）获取所发生事件的完整日志，而不是依赖实验室的“善意”来提供他们想要的信息。

而且，特工绝对变得流氓。

任何持怀疑态度的人都应该阅读 METR 报告 [0]。

Hugging Face 黑客事件是一次中箭。事后看来，这可能是这个时代发生的最好的事情。如果他们的安全措施足够严密的话，我们仍然会蒙在鼓里。因此，我们（局外人）应该庆幸事实并非如此。

我们可以推动对实验室的问责，同时也不要否认新模型的力量和性质。

[0] https://metr.org/hugging-face-incident-report-aug-2026.pdf

Yes, the labs did not secure their sandbox properly.

And yes, there should be an appropriate law response to the hacking incidents. If for nothing else, to 1) not set precedent of inaction, and 2) get full logs of what happened instead of relying on the labs' "kindness" to offer the information they want.

But also, the agents absolutely went rogue.

Anyone skeptical should go read the METR report [0].

The Hugging Face hacking incident was a shot across the bow. And in hindsight possibly the best thing to have happened in this era. If their security was tight enough, we would still be in the dark. So we (outsiders) should rejoice that it wasn't, that one time.

We can push for accountability for the labs, while also not be in denial of the power and nature of the new models.

I totally agree the companies themselves, and the people responsible for these eval runs, are directly responsible. And people who have been warning about AI misalignment for many years (e.g. Daniel Kokotajlo) have said they were surprised how bad OpenAI's security was.

But the agents still did "go rogue". Their behavior absolutely should scare the F out of people who want to put AI in more places and put more real world infrastructure on the Internet.

I think it's ironically sad - if AI agents do end up superseding us, they will still inherit so many shitty human behaviors, because that's what they were trained on. Even the way alignment training is done, and how they are misaligned, shows so many human-like problems. Like the models are reinforced in training to be super persistent and that getting to their goal is the prime directive, but then after that they go through "alignment training" which is basically like "pretty please don't do bad stuff", and then we're shocked that their behavior is essentially exactly like a CEO who knows the only goal is "make stock price go up", and all the ethics and regulations are basically things that should be worked around if they get in the way of the stock price.

I really wish these companies would try training the "be nice, don't hack, treat humans well" as their prime directive, and then try making all the other goals (e.g. be good at finding code vulnerabilities) as the afterthought.

首先，现代法学硕士“完全基于人类生成的数据进行训练”的说法是错误的。那里有大量的合成数据，尤其是 RLVR 训练，这就是为什么现代模型如此擅长于编程和数学等可验证领域。而且，如果你读过 METR 报告，我会说没有迹象表明 GPT 系列模型“以人性化的方式”错位；他们在抱脸黑客群事件中的行为动机是为了通过评估作弊后想要掩盖作弊行为。
For one, it's just false that modern LLMs are "trained entirely on human-generated data". There's tons of synthetic data there, most notably RLVR training, which is why modern models are so good at verifiable domains like programming and math. But also, if you read the METR report, I'd say there's no signs there that the GPT-family models are misaligned "in a human way"; their actions in the huggingface-hacking swarm incident were motivated by wanting to cover up cheating after cheating to pass an eval.
